note: Ugalde began her legal career in private practice in the litigation department of the Florida firm Akerman, Senterfitt & Eidson before joining the University of Miami as assistant general counsel in 1994; she became the university's first woman and first Hispanic general counsel in 2006 and is now Senior Vice President and General Counsel. Alongside that role she has served on the board of the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts Trust, chairing it from 2020.

name: Aimee Heeter
note: Heeter spent 23 years at Indiana University in budget and finance roles, rising from assistant vice president for budget to associate vice provost for finance and budget and then vice provost for finance and administration, where she oversaw the flagship campus's $2 billion budget. She became the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's first vice chancellor for finance in August 2025. All three of her degrees are from Indiana University and no employment outside higher education appears in her bio.

name: Ainsley A. Goulbourne

ties.title: Office of the Chief of Staff and CFO

note: Goulbourne spent roughly a decade at NYU Langone Health in the Office of the Chief of Staff and CFO, managing multimillion-dollar operations and research budgets and helping establish its Institute for Health Equity, then served as Chief Operating and Administrative Officer at the New York Academy of Sciences. He became Vice President for Finance and Administration and CFO at Southwestern University in November 2025.

name: Aisha Jackson
note: Jackson has spent more than 20 years in higher education technology: an ICT trainer and then lecturer at the University of the West Indies in Trinidad and Tobago (2005-2010), twelve years at the University of Colorado Boulder rising to assistant vice provost and assistant vice chancellor for academic technology, vice chancellor for information technology at UC Santa Cruz from 2022, and UC Davis's first chief information and digital strategy executive from December 2025. She taught before that but no named non-academic employer appears in her bios.

name: Akilah Rosado
note: Rosado worked for ten years in the New York State Assembly and then as an organizational and leadership development consultant with the Public Strategies Group before moving into higher education administration. She was Vice President for Governance, Social Justice, Equity and Inclusion at Bank Street College of Education, then Chief Equity and Diversity Officer and later Chief Transformation Officer at Relay Graduate School of Education, before joining Barnard College.

name: Al Checcio
note: Checcio has more than 40 years in fundraising and philanthropy, leading campaigns at American University, the University of Pittsburgh, Drexel University, Fordham University and USC, where he was senior vice president for advancement. Outside higher education he served as vice president of development at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. He was named Temple University's senior vice president of institutional advancement in September 2025.

name: Al Sturgeon
note: Before entering higher education administration, Sturgeon spent twelve years as a full-time preaching minister at two Churches of Christ, the Ocean Springs Church of Christ in Mississippi and later the University Church of Christ in Malibu, and led Hurricane Katrina recovery work on the Gulf Coast. He then earned a JD at Pepperdine and moved into student life roles at Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, Lipscomb, Blackburn and Ripon.

name: Alaina Gilligo

ties.firm: New York City Office of the Comptroller
ties.title: Chief Operating Officer / First Deputy Comptroller

ties.firm: Office of the Manhattan Borough President
ties.title: Chief of Staff

note: Gilligo came to Baruch in 2023 after roughly nineteen years as a New York City public-sector executive, most recently as Chief Operating Officer and First Deputy Comptroller in the NYC Comptroller's Office, where she oversaw climate-risk strategy for the city's retirement systems portfolio. Earlier she was chief of staff to the Manhattan Borough President. Baruch is her first university post.

name: Alan Schomaker

ties.title: Senior Database and PeopleSoft System Administrator

note: Schomaker spent just over a decade as an IT analyst, programmer and product manager for private companies before moving into healthcare IT at East Jefferson General Hospital in 1998. He joined LSU Health Sciences Center in 2001, rose to IT Director for Database and Support Services, and became CIO at Loyola New Orleans in February 2021.

name: Alan Thibeault
note: UNE's staff profile describes only his current duties as Vice President for University Operations and notes a UNE staff award in 1998, indicating a long tenure at the institution, but no published source documents his employment before UNE. No usable career bio covering the period before UNE could be located.

name: Alex Najera
note: Najera's HR career alternates between universities and local government: after starting as an admissions recruiter at CSU San Bernardino he held HR posts with the City of Indio, the County of Riverside and the Inland Empire Utilities Agency, then returned to higher education at CSUSB and UC Riverside. UCR named him Associate Vice Chancellor and CHRO effective October 2022.

name: Alex Perez
note: Perez began his legal career as an associate in the general practice group at Sullivan & Cromwell LLP in New York before moving in-house to the Rutgers University Office of the General Counsel. He later served as senior vice chancellor and chief of staff at Rutgers-New Brunswick and became SVP and general counsel at The New School in 2023.

name: Alexa Konstantinos
note: Konstantinos spent more than twenty years as a corporate marketing and communications executive, most recently as vice president of marketing at the healthcare software company CoverMyMeds, where she led a corporate brand consolidation across five merged businesses. She moved into higher education in January 2024 as vice president for marketing and communications at The College of Wooster.

name: Alexander E. McQuilkin

ties.firm: The Lundquist Institute for Biomedical Innovation at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center
ties.title: Vice President, Capital Projects and Facilities Management

note: McQuilkin is a career construction and capital projects manager with roughly 35 years of experience, including roles at the architecture and engineering firms CannonDesign and gkkworks and a stint as vice president for capital projects and facilities management at the nonprofit Lundquist Institute for Biomedical Innovation at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center from 2015 to 2019. He also worked for The Claremont Colleges Services before becoming associate vice president for facilities management at Binghamton University.

key: alexander r. miller|washington and lee university
name: Alexander R. Miller
note: Miller's employment history is entirely in university student affairs — Michigan State, Syracuse, Tulane, DePaul, the University of Chicago, Harvard, then Denison before Washington and Lee. His one non-academic affiliation is service on the board of trustees of Licking Memorial Hospital in Newark, Ohio, held while he was at Denison.

name: Alexandra Keller
note: Keller is a film and media studies scholar who joined the Smith College faculty in 2000 and rose through internal roles — program director, department chair, director of the Kahn Institute, chair of Faculty Council — to dean of the college and vice president for campus life in 2022. Her published bio lists only Harvard (BA), NYU (PhD) and Smith, with no employment or board service outside academia.

name: Alexandra Schimmer

ties.firm: Office of the Ohio Attorney General
ties.title: Solicitor General of Ohio (previously Chief Deputy Solicitor General)

note: Schimmer is a lawyer who clerked for federal judges in New York and Ohio, practiced litigation and appellate law at the Vorys firm in Columbus, and then served the State of Ohio as Chief Deputy Solicitor General and Solicitor General, arguing cases in the U.S. Supreme Court and federal appellate courts. She moved into higher education as deputy general counsel at Ohio State before becoming VP and general counsel at Denison in 2019.

name: Alicia Estey
note: Estey worked in corporate tax at the agribusiness firm J.R. Simplot Company before joining Boise State University in 2006, where she spent nearly two decades in compliance, chief-of-staff and finance roles ending as CFO and vice president for finance and operations. Alongside that she served as an elected trustee of the Boise School District board; she became UVM's vice president for finance and administration in August 2025.

name: Alicia Lloyd
note: Lloyd began in student affairs at Grand Valley State University in 2005 as an academic advising graduate assistant and held roles there in the Dean of Students Office, Student Affairs and Multicultural Affairs, plus a stint in residence life at Miami University in Ohio, before moving to Aquinas College. Her published biography shows an unbroken campus career with no non-academic employer or board seat.

name: Alisa Macksey

ties.title: Interim Executive Director and Regional Programs Director
Director (previously Associate Director); earlier a volunteer

note: Macksey spent roughly fifteen years in the Lasallian nonprofit network before entering higher education administration — as a Lasallian Volunteer from 2000, then eight years on the Lasallian Volunteers staff as associate director and director, and finally regional programs director and interim executive director at the Christian Brothers Conference. She joined Saint Mary's University of Minnesota in 2015 and became vice president for mission, diversity and inclusion at La Salle University in 2022.

name: Alisa Robertson
note: Robertson has spent her entire documented 30-year career in service to UW-Madison, joining in 1997 as assistant director of alumni relations at the Wisconsin School of Business and rising to associate dean of advancement, then moving to the university's fundraising arm in 2011 as chief of staff and becoming its chief development officer, president and finally CEO. No employer outside the university and its affiliated foundation appears in her published biographies.

name: Alison Dougherty
note: Dougherty's career in human resources and Title IX compliance has been entirely on university campuses — Widener University, Saint Joseph's University, Drexel University and Lafayette College, with doctoral study at Northeastern. Lafayette's appointment announcement recites her full employment history and names no company, firm, agency or nonprofit.

name: Alison Harmon
note: Harmon is a registered dietitian nutritionist who came to Montana State University in 2004 from Pennsylvania State University, where she earned her doctorate and worked on sustainable food systems. At MSU she built the sustainable food and bioenergy systems programs and the state's first dietetic internship, becoming dean of the College of Education, Health and Human Development and later vice president for research; her published profiles list no non-academic employer or board seat.

name: Alison Miller
note: VCU's appointment announcement states that before entering higher education Miller held roles as a consulting partner, consulting principal and HR manager at state government agencies and private firms; professional listings identify the Richmond HR consultancy Titan Group as her employer in that period. She then spent four years as director of total rewards at the University of Virginia, joined VCU in 2017, and became chief human resources officer in July 2024.
